title: Imports and Dependencies
content: Imports Mathlib's SimpleGraph module for graph definitions, the Clique submodule for triangle detection, real number basics, logarithmic functions, and general tactics. The logarithm import is essential since the asymptotic formula involves $k^2 \log k$.
mathContext: Uses $\text{SimpleGraph}(\text{Fin}\, n)$ for finite graphs and $\text{Real.log}$ for the natural logarithm.

title: Triangle-Free Graph
content: A graph is triangle-free if it contains no clique of size 3, i.e., no three mutually adjacent vertices. This is the local structural constraint that makes achieving high chromatic number difficult: without triangles, one cannot use clique-based lower bounds on the chromatic number, and instead must rely on global structure. The definition quantifies over all triples of distinct vertices and requires that at least one pair is non-adjacent.
mathContext:
$G$ is triangle-free iff $

eq c$ with $ab, bc, ac \in E(G)$, equivalently $\omega(G) \leq 2$.

title: Proper k-Coloring
content: A proper k-coloring assigns one of k colors to each vertex such that no two adjacent vertices share the same color. This is formalized as a function $f: \text{Fin}\,n \to \text{Fin}\,k$ with the constraint $f(u) \neq f(v)$ whenever $G$ has an edge between $u$ and $v$. The chromatic number is the minimum k for which such a coloring exists.

title: Chromatic Number
content: The chromatic number $\chi(G)$ is defined as one more than the supremum of k values for which no proper k-coloring exists. This is a noncomputable definition since determining the chromatic number is NP-hard in general. For triangle-free graphs, the relationship between $\chi$ and the number of vertices is the central question.

title: Triangle-Free Chromatic Threshold h_3(k)
content: The function $h_3(k)$ is the smallest $n$ such that there exists a triangle-free graph on $n$ vertices with chromatic number at least $k$. Equivalently, it is the supremum of $m$ such that every triangle-free graph on fewer than $m$ vertices is $(k-1)$-colorable. This is the central quantity of Problem #1013. Mycielski's construction guarantees $h_3(k) < \infty$ for all $k$.

title: Asymptotic Conjecture: h_3(k) ~ c k^2 log k
content: The central conjecture asserts that $h_3(k)/(k^2 \log k)$ converges to a constant $c > 0$ as $k \to \infty$. The known bounds give $c \in [1/2, 1]$, leaving open whether the constant is exactly $1/2$, exactly $1$, or something in between. The formalization uses Lean's Filter.Tendsto to express the limit. Determining the exact constant would reveal how efficiently triangle-free graphs can force high chromatic number.

title: Ratio Convergence: h_3(k+1)/h_3(k) -> 1
content: Erdos asked whether the ratio of consecutive thresholds converges to 1, meaning $h_3$ grows smoothly without large jumps. If $h_3(k) \sim c k^2 \log k$, then $h_3(k+1)/h_3(k) \sim (k+1)^2 \log(k+1)/(k^2 \log k) \to 1$, so ratio convergence would follow from the asymptotic formula. However, ratio convergence could hold even without the full asymptotic, making it a potentially weaker statement.

title: Lower Bound: (1/2 - o(1)) k^2 log k
content: The lower bound asserts that any triangle-free graph on fewer than roughly $k^2 \log k / 2$ vertices is $(k-1)$-colorable. This is proved using probabilistic arguments: a random partition into classes of size about $k$ gives independent sets with high probability when the graph has few vertices. The factor $1/2$ arises from the entropy of the random coloring scheme.
mathContext: $\forall \varepsilon > 0,\, \exists K,\, \forall k \geq K: h_3(k) \geq (1/2 - \varepsilon) k^2 \ln k$.

title: Upper Bound: (1 + o(1)) k^2 log k
content: Explicit constructions of triangle-free graphs with chromatic number $k$ on roughly $k^2 \log k$ vertices establish the upper bound. These constructions include random graph methods (selecting triangle-free subgraphs of $G(n,p)$ with appropriate density), Ramsey-type constructions, and algebraic constructions based on finite fields.
mathContext: $\forall \varepsilon > 0,\, \exists K,\, \forall k \geq K: h_3(k) \leq (1 + \varepsilon) k^2 \ln k$.

title: Graver-Yackel (1968): Early Lower Bound
content: Graver and Yackel gave the first quantitative lower bound $h_3(k) \gg k^2 \log k / \log \log k$, weaker than the modern $k^2 \log k / 2$ by a $\log \log k$ factor. Their method used probabilistic deletion from random graphs. This historical result established the $k^2$ growth rate and motivated the search for the correct logarithmic factor.
mathContext: $h_3(k) \geq c \cdot k^2 \cdot \frac{\ln k}{\ln \ln k}$ for some $c > 0$ and large $k$.

title: Monotonicity of h_3
content: The threshold function $h_3$ is non-decreasing: if $j \leq k$, then $h_3(j) \leq h_3(k)$. This follows because any graph with chromatic number $\geq k$ also has chromatic number $\geq j$, so achieving higher chromatic number requires at least as many vertices.

title: Small Cases: h_3(1) through h_3(4)
content: The first few values are exactly known: $h_3(1)=1$ (trivial), $h_3(2)=2$ (need an edge for $\chi \geq 2$), $h_3(3)=5$ (the 5-cycle $C_5$ is the smallest triangle-free graph with $\chi = 3$), and $h_3(4)=11$ (the Grotzsch graph, which is the Mycielski graph $M_4$, has 11 vertices). These values are listed in OEIS A292528.

title: Mycielski's Construction
content: Mycielski (1955) gave an inductive construction: starting from $K_2$, each step adds a new layer of vertices and a universal vertex, increasing the chromatic number by 1 while preserving triangle-freeness. The Mycielski graph $M_k$ has $3 \cdot 2^{k-2} - 1$ vertices and chromatic number $k$. This proves $h_3(k) < \infty$ for all $k$, establishing that the function $h_3$ is well-defined. The construction gives $h_3(k) \leq 3 \cdot 2^{k-2} - 1$, but the true growth is only $\Theta(k^2 \log k)$.
